newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seen facing more grain supply problems.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seen facing more grain supply problems.

text.p: Bulgaria may face fresh grain supply problems this year as the cash-strapped production sector is not being stimulated and prices need to be liberalised, farm analysts said on Thursday.

"The grain producers are under severe pressure and the country may face a new grain crisis as the administrative measures of the cabinet will have only a short term effect," the head of the Institute for Agricultural Economics (IAE), Ranguel Trendafilov, told a news conference.
Bulgaria has negotiated deals to import wheat immediately against exports from the next harvest.

"It is obvious that the country needs to import wheat immediately but this is not the solution to Bulgaria's problems as the only way out of the crisis is an intensive development of the production units," Trendafilov said.

"I do not see how the cabinet will force the farmers to sell their grain at the initially estimated price of 45,000 levs per tonne because this will not even cover production costs and after exports of the contracted volumes of wheat we may end 1997 with a new grains crisis," Trendafilov said.
The price was proposed by the state buyer earlier this year.
The IAE has issued a draft programme to solve the problem in the next four to five years.

"There are always two sides in a market economy -- producers and consumers -- and the only effective way out of the current crisis is to support the producers by liberalising grain prices on the domestic market and lifting all bans on imports and exports," IAE senior researcher Yanka Slavova said.
The IAE sees domestic wheat production at 4.5 million tonnes by the end of the century, against an estimated 3.5 million this year, if grain prices are liberalised.
